title: Leviticus Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Leviticus 5: confessing sin, offerings for those who cannot afford a lamb, and the trespass offering.

questions.text: Which of these makes a person guilty, even when it was hidden from him?
questions.explanation: If anyone touches any unclean thing, such as the carcass of an unclean animal, and it is hidden from him, and he is unclean, then he shall be guilty.

answers.text: Touching the carcass of an unclean animal
Eating unleavened bread at the feast
Washing his clothes in running water
Sleeping outside the camp

questions.text: What must a person do when he is guilty of one of these sins?
questions.explanation: When he is guilty of one of these, he shall confess that in which he has sinned.

answers.text: Fast for seven days
Confess the sin he has committed
Shave his head and his beard
Stay outside the camp until evening

questions.text: What was the guilty person to bring as his trespass offering for a sin offering?
questions.explanation: He shall bring a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering.

answers.text: A young bull from the herd
A male goat without defect
A female from the flock, a lamb or a goat
A tenth of an ephah of barley

questions.text: What could someone bring if he could not afford a lamb?
questions.explanation: If he can't afford a lamb, he shall bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to Yahweh.

answers.text: A young male goat
A jar of olive oil for the lamp
Five shekels of silver for the priest
Two turtledoves or two young pigeons

questions.text: What was done with the two birds?
questions.explanation: One was for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.

answers.text: Both were burned as burnt offerings
One was a sin offering and the other a burnt offering
One was offered and the other set free
Both were given to the priest to eat

questions.text: How was the head of the bird for the sin offering handled?
questions.explanation: The priest shall wring off its head from its neck, but shall not sever it completely.

answers.text: It was wrung at the neck but not severed completely
It was cut off and thrown into the fire
It was left untouched
It was cut off completely and buried outside the camp

questions.text: How much fine flour could someone bring if he could not even afford two birds?
questions.explanation: He shall bring one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering.

answers.text: A whole ephah of flour
Half an ephah
Two handfuls of flour
One tenth of an ephah

questions.text: Why was no oil or frankincense to be put on that fine flour?
questions.explanation: He shall put no oil on it, and he shall not put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.

answers.text: Because oil was too costly
Because the priest would add them later
Because it is a sin offering
Because it was offered in the evening

questions.text: What must someone add when making restitution for a wrong regarding Yahweh's holy things?
questions.explanation: He shall make restitution for that which he has done wrong regarding the holy thing, and shall add a fifth part to it, and give it to the priest.

answers.text: A fifth part
A tenth part
Double the amount
Half the amount

questions.text: What does the text say about someone who does a forbidden thing without knowing it?
questions.explanation: Though he didn't know it, he is still guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

answers.text: He is not guilty at all
He is still guilty and shall bear his iniquity
He is only unclean until evening
He must stay outside the camp for seven days
